_source: output/tables/estimates_v1.md, from the src/06_estimate.R run confirmed in VALIDATION_REPORT.md/PROJECT_PLAN.md. Hand-transcribed once; 06_estimate.R now also writes this file directly on any future run.
outcome: rejection_rate (rejected_total / returned_by_voters), usable & in-scope (50 states + DC) jurisdiction-years, 2016-2024

models.label: Naive two-way fixed effects
models.note: Fixed effects: fips (6,367 levels) + year. Clustered SEs by state; bootstrap = wild-cluster (fwildclusterboot, B=999).

models.label: Sun & Abraham (2021) interaction-weighted
models.note: Excludes Iowa (treatment reversal) and 13 always-treated states (no pre-period to identify an event-time effect from).

models.label: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) doubly-robust
models.note: Same exclusions as Sun-Abraham. Control group: never-treated. Estimation method: doubly robust.

headline: All three estimators independently give a clean null. Point estimates bounce between +0.0024 and -0.0045 (about a quarter to half a percentage point of rejection rate either way), but every confidence interval comfortably contains zero and every p-value is well above 0.05 -- there is no evidence in this design that mandatory signature-cure notice laws changed mail ballot rejection rates.
